equivalents.plural: mugs of water boiled in a kettle

source.title: Water, condensed phase thermochemistry data, liquid phase heat capacity (Shomate equation)
source.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology, Chemistry WebBook

provenance.note: Worked out, not quoted. The page's Shomate coefficients give 75.37 J/mol K at 298 K, which is 4.184 J/g K. Taking 300 mL from 10 to 100 degrees is 300 x 4.184 x 90 = 112,968 J, or 31.4 Wh. We add a tenth for heat lost from the kettle, our assumption, which gives 35 Wh. The old figure of 100 Wh was recalled, not sourced, and made a prompt look three times smaller next to a mug than it is.

equivalents.notes: Seventeen years old and quoted constantly. We keep it because the comparison is the one people reach for, and we mark it stale wherever it appears.
